---
title: "PROC MEANS: log, listing and HTML output"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Show an HTML document of sas_html() in an isolated frame, so its style
# sheet does not mix with the page.
show_html <- function(doc, height = 320) {
  esc <- gsub('"', "&quot;", gsub("&", "&amp;", doc, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf(
    '<iframe srcdoc="%s" style="width: 100%%; height: %dpx; border: 1px solid #c1c1c1;"></iframe>',
    esc, height))
}
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

A procedure step has three outputs in sasonr while the HTML destination is
open:

* the **log**: the program lines with the NOTEs of each step;
* the **listing**: the procedure output as text, laid out at `LINESIZE`;
* the **HTML** document: the same tables with the blue-and-grey style of the
  HTML destination.

PROC MEANS builds its output once, as ODS tables (`sasonr_ods_table`); the
listing and the HTML document are both rendered from these tables, so they
always show the same numbers. This article uses one small invented data set
throughout.

## The program

```{r}
res <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ visit week aval;
  datalines;
A 1 0 10.2
A 1 4 11.8
A 2 0 9.6
A 2 4 12.1
B 1 0 10.9
B 1 4 10.4
B 2 0 11.3
B 2 4 9.8
;
run;

title 'Change from baseline';
proc means data=trial n mean std min max maxdec=2;
  class arm week;
  var aval;
run;
")
```

## The log

`sas_log()` gives the program lines with their numbers and the NOTEs of
each step:

```{r}
sas_log(res)
```

`sas_log(res, echo = FALSE)` keeps only the messages; in a terminal with
colours, `print(res)` shows NOTEs in blue, WARNINGs in green and ERRORs in
red. The same log as HTML:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show_html(paste0("<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\"><style>",
                 paste(readLines(system.file("css", "sasonr.css", package = "sasonr")), collapse = "\n"),
                 "</style></head><body>", sas_log(res, format = "html"), "</body></html>"),
          height = 380)
```

## The listing

`$listing` holds the procedure output as text, with the title, the procedure
title, the CLASS columns and the statistic columns laid out at `LINESIZE`
(MAXDEC=2 here):

```{r}
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
```

## The HTML output

`sas_html()` writes the procedure output of a result as an HTML document:
one table per ODS table, under the titles. The document embeds its style
sheet (`system.file("css", "sasonr.css", package = "sasonr")`):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sas_html(res, file = "means.html")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show_html(sas_html(res), height = 330)
```

`sas_html(res, log = TRUE)` adds the log after the tables. The HTML
destination is open when a program starts; `ODS HTML CLOSE;` closes it (the
tables of the following steps are left out of the document) and `ODS HTML;`
opens it again.

## BY groups

With a BY statement each BY group gets its own table under a BY line, in
the listing and in the HTML document:

```{r}
res_by <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ visit week aval;
  datalines;
A 1 0 10.2
A 1 4 11.8
A 2 0 9.6
A 2 4 12.1
B 1 0 10.9
B 1 4 10.4
B 2 0 11.3
B 2 4 9.8
;
run;
proc sort data=trial; by arm; run;
title 'Analysis value by arm';
proc means data=trial n mean maxdec=1;
  by arm;
  var aval;
run;
")
cat(res_by$listing, sep = "\n")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show_html(sas_html(res_by), height = 380)
```

## The ODS tables

`$ods` holds the ODS tables of a result in output order. Each is a tibble of
the raw values (numbers unformatted) with the table's name, label, path,
BY values and column headers as attributes:

```{r}
tab <- res$ods[[1]]
attr(tab, "name")
attr(tab, "path")
tab
```

## ODS OUTPUT: the table as a data set

`ODS OUTPUT Summary=<data set>;` before the PROC MEANS step writes the
Summary table to WORK, with the usual data set NOTE in the log:

```{r}
res_out <- sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ aval;
  datalines;
A 10.2
A 11.8
B 10.9
B 10.4
;
run;
ods output Summary=stats;
proc means data=trial n mean;
  class arm;
  var aval;
run;
")
sas_log(res_out, echo = FALSE)
res_out$work$stats
```

## Procedures on data frames

`sas_means_df()`, `sas_tabulate_df()`, `sas_freq_df()` (one-way tables) and
`sas_transpose_df()` run one
procedure on a data frame without a program. They read their arguments
with the same parser and specification builder as the PROC step of a
program and call the same computation, so the table is the one the program
gives. `as.data.frame()` drops the table attributes; `sas_log()` gives the
WARNINGs and NOTEs of the computation and `sas_html()` the HTML document.

```{r}
d <- data.frame(arm = c("A", "A", "B", "B"), aval = c(10.2, 11.8, 10.9, 10.4))
m <- sas_means_df(d, var = "aval", class = "arm", stats = c("n", "mean"))
as.data.frame(m)
as.data.frame(sas_tabulate_df(d, "arm all, aval*(n mean)", class = "arm", var = "aval"))
as.data.frame(sas_freq_df(d, "arm"))
```

## The RTF document

`ODS RTF FILE="path";` opens the RTF destination; the PROC PRINT and PROC
TABULATE tables of the steps that follow go into the document, which is
written at `ODS RTF CLOSE;`. The document follows the default RTF style: a
heading row repeated on every page, row titles and headings in bold, merged
row titles, BY lines, and the column widths of that style.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sas_run("
data trial;
  input arm $ aval;
  datalines;
A 10
B 11
;
run;
ods rtf file=\"trial.rtf\";
proc print data=trial;
run;
ods rtf close;
")
```

## What fails loud

sasonr stops with a `sasonr_unsupported` condition, naming the SAS line,
for output requests it does not implement: `ODS HTML FILE=` and the other
ODS HTML options (write the document with `sas_html(file = )` instead),
`ODS OUTPUT` with MATCH_ALL, PERSIST= or BY groups, the ODS actions (CLOSE,
SELECT, EXCLUDE, ...), and FOOTNOTE statements in the HTML document. `sas_html()` also stops when the HTML destination received output that has
no HTML view yet (PROC PRINT, PROC FREQ statistics other than CHISQ) (close the destination around
those steps with `ODS HTML CLOSE;` to get the document of the others).
